comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations support the GDNF overexpression model characterization (C2, C25-C40). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment of experimental approaches, while peer reviewers implicitly accept the model as part of their overall positive evaluation.

Strong agreement on RNAseq discovery of EOMES (C41-C56). OpenEval supports the experimental design and statistical approach, noting C54 and C56 are speculative. Peer reviewers accept the identification as a key finding. Peer result includes C3 not in OpenEval result, but both evaluations are supportive.

Complete agreement. Both evaluations support the immunofluorescence characterization of EOMES expression patterns (C57-C67). OpenEval provides detailed technical assessment, while peer reviewers accept the protein expression data without concerns.

Strong agreement on lineage tracing evidence for SSC function (C68-C79). OpenEval supports the experimental design and functional evidence. Peer reviewers accept the labeling experiments as demonstrating SSC characteristics. Peer result includes C4 and C128 not in OpenEval result.

Agreement on busulfan resistance data (C81-C89). Both evaluations support the functional evidence for SSC identity. OpenEval notes C86 is speculative about mechanism. Peer reviewers accept this as convincing functional characterization. OpenEval includes C80 not in peer result.

Significant disagreement. Both address proliferation data (C5, C90-C94). OpenEval supports the proliferation findings with minor concerns about mechanistic interpretations. Peer reviewers question whether the data convincingly demonstrate slow-cycling and recommend removing such references (Essential revision #1).

Partial disagreement on proliferative exhaustion model (C6-C7, C129-C130, C161-C162, C168-C170). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the model is largely speculative and based on analogy rather than direct evidence. Peer reviewers also express uncertainty, particularly as it relates to the questioned slow-cycling claim.

Agreement on scRNA-seq heterogeneity findings (C8, C95-C113, C135-C136). OpenEval supports the comprehensive analysis and heterogeneity conclusions despite noting cluster 1 has limited cells. Peer reviewers accept the heterogeneity and plasticity findings. Peer result includes C141 and excludes some technical claims (C102, C104, C110) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Agreement on scRNA-seq analysis of PLZF mutant effects (C114-C118). OpenEval supports the comparative analysis with minor concerns about C118 interpretation. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the overall heterogeneity characterization, though they group this with broader scRNA-seq results.

Agreement on ID4 expression validation (C119-C126, C153-C154). OpenEval supports the data with appropriate controls, noting some speculation about GFP/protein discordance. Peer reviewers accept the findings and suggest additional characterization comparing EOMES in ID4 bright vs dim cells. Peer result includes additional claims (C148-C152, C155-C156) about ID4 in broader context.

Both address technical limitations of scRNA-seq (C102, C104, C110). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting fundamental uncertainty about cell purity. Peer reviewers implicitly accept the approach as part of their overall support for heterogeneity findings, though they don't explicitly address these technical concerns.

Agreement that interpretations are speculative. OpenEval rates heterogeneous EOMES expression claims (C131-C134) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of mechanistic evidence. Peer reviewers accept the descriptive findings and discussion of plasticity implications, suggesting they view these as appropriate speculation rather than definitive claims.

Agreement on spatial organization observations (C138-C140). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting C140 is entirely speculative about mechanism. Peer reviewers accept the descriptive findings as supporting plasticity understanding, treating the mechanistic speculation as discussion rather than unsupported claims.

Partial overlap on integration with prior literature (C141-C152, C156). OpenEval supports the synthesis with published data while noting some limitations. Peer reviewers focus on ID4-related claims (C148-C152, C156) and suggest additional characterization, accepting the current integration.

Agreement on speculative nature. OpenEval rates fragmentation model reconciliation (C157-C159) as UNCERTAIN, noting the hypothesis is not directly tested. Peer reviewers accept the discussion of plasticity and stemness states, suggesting they view this as appropriate contextualization of findings.

OpenEval evaluated background and contextual claims (C1, C9-C24, C31, C34, C39, C46, C48, C50, C62, C137, C160, C163-C167) as SUPPORTED based on appropriate citations. Peer reviewers did not separately evaluate these background claims, focusing instead on novel experimental findings.
